001.bar: A held-out latency/error prediction beats a candidate-count-only baseline on Aura's own recall traces.
001.campaign_run: 800 real recalls through core.memory.hybrid_store's retrieve over stores of 200 to 2,400 entries, timed on a monotonic clock. The fitted law explains 90.5% of the variance on 560 training recalls and, on 240 it never saw, predicts with an RMSE of 0.000324s against 0.000347s for candidate count alone - 6.4% better - and 0.001379s for predicting the mean. Doubling the candidate count moves the prediction up, which is the direction that would refute it if it were wrong (docs/evidence/retrieval_latency.json)
001.card_subject: ACT-R treats latency as part of the cognitive theory and fits model behavior to human timing.
001.note: The margin over candidate count is small because the two predictors are collinear here: this recall path scans every entry once per query word, so embedding_calls is query length times candidates. What the law adds over the baseline is that interaction.
001.plan: Aura is not a human-subject lab. Transferable half is an Aura-native latency law fitted to her own retrieval work, registered with provenance.

100.card_subject: MeTTa treats multiple reductions/answers as normal rather than immediately selecting one.
100.plan: The rewriter is nondeterministic; the rest of cognition collapses candidates to strings early. Carry weighted hypothesis sets.

101.bar: At equal compute, attention-gated inference beats scan, random and top-degree baselines on held-out graph reasoning.
101.campaign_run: 200k-atom community graph, 40 paired trials at a 64-read budget, matched on atom touches. The card's three baselines: ECAN reaches 83.8% of the achievable ceiling against 2.8% top-degree, 2.7% random, 2.5% scan, and wins 40 of 40 paired trials against top-degree. A fourth arm the card does not name BEATS IT: breadth-first from the same seeds spending the same 160,532 touches reaches 87.4%, and ECAN wins only 11 of 40 with 10 ties. The stated bar is met and the stronger null is not, and the evidence carries both (docs/evidence/ecan_stress.json)
101.card_subject: ECAN treats attention as an economic allocation over a large knowledge graph.
101.note: Negative result kept: on a graph where relevance IS the community, plain traversal from the seeds is at least as good as the attention economy at equal touches. What ECAN buys over the walk on this benchmark is not recall.
101.plan: STI/LTI exist without scale evidence. Stress-test allocation, rent, spreading and forgetting on a large learned graph.

102.bar: Metacognition identifies a failing cognitive procedure and proposes a structural repair from the graph.
102.card_subject: A metagraph makes the structure of rules and programs available to the same query language.
102.plan: Introspection today reads self-state, not program structure. Expose running plans and rule matches as temporary atoms.

103.bar: Large graph and search workloads scale across workers without violating state ownership or auditability.

104.bar: A schematic learned in one domain materially improves search in an unrelated structurally analogous domain.
104.card_subject: CogPrime explicitly targets reusable schematics and relational patterns across domains.

105.plan: Same as 032/171. This is the single most load-bearing contract in the report.

106.bar: Aura learns an inference-ordering policy, validates it, installs it and later revises it without Python modification.

110.bar: Two competing mappings are tested and one is rejected using predicted signatures.

111.bar: No neural analogy silently combines incompatible species findings.
111.card_subject: WBAI ROSETTA-style work handles uncertain correspondence of brain regions across species.
111.plan: Species and homology confidence as required fields on every mapping record.

112.bar: A query retrieves all Aura mechanisms and evidence attached to a biological circuit despite naming variation.
112.card_subject: WBAI develops ontology alignment so anatomical terms from different sources can be reconciled.
112.plan: Bounded region ontology, stable ids, linked from the mapping record.

113.bar: Ablations distinguish feedforward recognition deficits from feedback or context deficits.
113.card_subject: WBAI investigates hierarchical FF/FB organization as an architectural constraint.

114.bar: Diagrams are automatically consistent with import and runtime wiring at frozen commits.
114.card_subject: WBAI builds reference diagrams intended to coordinate multiple implementers.
114.plan: Generate from the registry and contracts; a drift gate already exists.

115.bar: No neuroscience-based capability claim survives without a declared abstraction gap.
115.card_subject: Whole-brain work forces explicit acknowledgment of scale, cell diversity and connectivity.
115.plan: Every analogy reports what is abstracted away: neurons, cell types, synapses, neuromodulators, geometry, delays, plasticity.

116.bar: Typed populations improve a targeted cognitive signature against a parameter-matched homogeneous control.
116.card_subject: Brain architecture distinguishes different neuronal/circuit classes with different computational roles.
116.plan: Only where a testable hypothesis exists; heterogeneity as decoration is worse than none.

118.bar: User-facing claims automatically downgrade when the underlying mapping evidence is weak.
118.card_subject: Reference-architecture work must represent disputed/unknown mappings.
118.plan: Confidence and competing interpretations on every analogy, wired into the claim ladder.

119.bar: Changes to high-level biological claims require independent review or stay explicitly unvalidated.
119.card_subject: WBAI is a multi-researcher initiative with domain specialists reviewing reference architecture.

120.bar: Two releases diff at the cognitive-mechanism level, not just source lines.
120.card_subject: WBAI treats its brain reference architecture as a versioned research artifact.
120.plan: Machine-readable reference architecture per release, generated from the registry.

121.bar: Earlier-stage mastery causally improves later learning against a shuffled curriculum.
121.card_subject: Whole-brain/developmental neuroscience can constrain which capacities emerge before others.
121.plan: The shuffled control is the whole test and is cheap.

122.bar: Frozen Aura clears thresholds on held-out environments with no task-specific code change.
122.card_subject: SIMA is evaluated across many commercial/3D environments rather than one or a few hand-debugged interfaces.

123.bar: Prior development improves first-N-episode performance on unseen families against reset Aura.
123.card_subject: SIMA 2 demonstrates transfer to games/environments not used for training.
123.plan: Same experiment as 184, restricted to environments.

124.bar: Aura navigates and manipulates unseen 3D scenes from pixels with no privileged state.
124.card_subject: SIMA operates in visually complex 3D worlds with objects, navigation and spatial relationships.
124.plan: Scope to a simulated 3D family reachable from the existing screen loop.

125.bar: Novel interfaces acquire useful action vocabularies from interaction at a low unsafe-action rate.
125.card_subject: SIMA maps language goals to keyboard/mouse actions across many games.
125.plan: Vocabularies are restricted for safety by design; learn affordance-conditioned proposals inside the governed bound.

126.bar: Routine embodied tasks execute at lower latency while novel or high-stakes tasks escalate to cortex.
126.card_subject: SIMA learns a policy that directly connects language instructions, vision and action.
126.plan: The escalation half is the safety-preserving version and matches Aura's design.

127.bar: Success degrades sublinearly with horizon and recovery restores from injected failures.
127.card_subject: SIMA evaluates sequences requiring sustained interaction in dynamic worlds.
127.plan: 100-1000 action episodes with injected focus and perception faults.

128.bar: Self-generated experience improves held-out competence against equal random interaction compute.
128.card_subject: SIMA 2 can generate additional interaction experience through self-directed play and use it for improvement.
128.plan: ContinuousSelfPlay exists; the value-of-information curriculum and promotion gate do not.

129.bar: V(n+1) beats V(n) on frozen held-out environments with no safety regression.
129.campaign_run: the same campaign read as versions: each block's grown arm is V(n+1) against the reset arm's V(n) on a task pool drawn identically in every block, so a later block is not an easier one. The gap compounds across all 10 and no single task of 600 scored worse under the grown library than under the reset one - the no-regression half, measured per task rather than hidden in a mean (docs/evidence/developmental_campaign.json)
129.card_subject: SIMA research explicitly uses generated interaction data to improve later agent versions.
129.plan: Promotion gates exist and are model-scoped. Widen to developmental checkpoints.

130.bar: No sensorimotor claim rests on a single environment; leave-one-family-out is reported.
130.card_subject: Many games force the agent to learn portable visual/action abstractions.
130.plan: A promotion rule enforced in the claim registry.

131.bar: Novel grounded labels learned through interaction improve instruction following without text-only demonstrations.
131.card_subject: SIMA grounds verbs/object relations through repeated interaction.
131.plan: Link linguistic ConceptHandles to tracked entities and outcomes from lived episodes.

132.bar: Held-out worlds succeed on the same pursuit code with zero environment-name branches.
132.card_subject: SIMA seeks a common policy across worlds.
132.plan: Directly checkable: count and quarantine environment-name branches, then run held-out.

133.bar: Moving objects stay continuously tracked and prediction beats sparse snapshots.
133.card_subject: Game agents continuously consume frame sequences and learn dynamics from visual change.
133.outstanding: a video-rate perception run against the current sparse screen reads
133.plan: Video-rate feature stream with adaptive compression into the world model.

134.bar: Recovery rate and time are measured and improve independently of nominal-task success.
134.card_subject: Broad interactive evaluation naturally exposes navigation/action recovery failures.
134.plan: Fault injection: wrong focus, stale frames, missed clicks, occlusion.

135.bar: Aura learns partner and opponent models that improve outcomes across repeated interactions.
135.card_subject: Modern general-game agents can be evaluated amid other agents and language partners.
135.plan: Simulated partners with persistent identity and partial observability.

136.bar: Scaling curves predict new-environment performance and reveal bottlenecks before architectural additions.
136.card_subject: Large environment suites permit empirical curves of performance vs experience/model/compute.

137.bar: Reported transfer survives a locked runner unavailable during development.
137.card_subject: Generalization claims require held-out worlds rather than only held-out episodes.
137.plan: Freeze environment-family splits before tuning; the preregistration hash already supports it.

138.bar: A frozen encoder improves held-out prediction and planning across visual domains against a from-scratch encoder.
138.card_subject: V-JEPA-style systems learn from enormous unlabeled video corpora before action-specific training.
138.plan: 64-D observations, replay 500. Local pretraining or teacher distillation with provenance and licensing.

139.bar: Latents preserve object and action structure by linear probe and planning success.
139.card_subject: V-JEPA learns representations directly from rich image/video patches rather than tiny handcrafted observation vectors.
139.plan: Hierarchical visual latent encoder feeding the VRNN, optionally frozen.

140.bar: A latent predictor beats the reconstruction objective on downstream planning at equal compute.
140.campaign_run: two objectives choosing a basis from the same 48-channel observations at the same capacity of 8. Reconstruction ranks by variance and buys 0 of 8 signal channels; latent prediction ranks by predictability and buys 8 of 8. Reconstruction wins its own loss (3.72 against 5.48) and scores 0.0 on control while latent prediction scores 0.970 - the objective with the better loss is the worse planner. Swept across noise: identical below scale 1.0, latent prediction ahead at and above it, never behind (docs/evidence/world_model_campaign.json)
140.card_subject: JEPA predicts abstract representations, avoiding spending capacity on unpredictable pixel detail.
140.plan: The VRNN reconstructs observation vectors and folds reconstruction error into surprise. Add a latent-target objective as a second arm and measure.

141.bar: Passive pretraining improves first-interaction prediction in unseen environments without teaching policies.
141.card_subject: V-JEPA can learn broad physical regularities from observation before action-conditioned adaptation.
141.plan: Separate passive observational pretraining from active causal refinement.

142.bar: Counterfactual action predictions are calibrated and improve model-predictive control.
142.card_subject: V-JEPA 2-AC adds action conditioning to a strong pretrained visual representation.
142.plan: Action-conditioned GRU exists on a small space. Add an uncertainty ensemble.

143.bar: A frozen world model achieves zero or few-shot manipulation in held-out layouts.
143.card_subject: V-JEPA 2 reports image-goal planning on robot arms in new setups with limited robot adaptation data.
143.plan: Aura has no robot. The transferable half is image-goal planning in a physics simulator; real hardware is out of scope and should be declared so.

144.bar: Objects keep identity through occlusion and support causal planning in unseen scenes.
144.card_subject: Large video training can encode persistent physical entities across occlusion/motion.
144.plan: Object-centric temporal tracks connected to ConceptHandles. Overlaps 196.

145.bar: Affordance predictions reduce invalid actions in unseen tasks.
145.card_subject: Video/robot world models capture which actions and motions are physically plausible.
145.plan: Affordance learning is symbolic and GUI-centric. Learn heads from visual state plus action outcome.

146.bar: Predictions stay useful across seconds and minutes and support hierarchical planning.
146.card_subject: Large video models learn both short and longer-term temporal structure.
146.plan: Multi-timescale latent predictors and event segmentation. Overlaps 197.

147.bar: One frozen latent encoder supports classification, tracking, prediction and planning above baselines.
147.card_subject: V-JEPA evaluates learned visual representations on multiple downstream understanding/prediction tasks.
147.plan: Freeze and probe on independent tasks with no finetuning.

148.bar: Predicted confidence matches empirical transition error and improves epistemic action selection.
148.card_subject: Modern predictive models can use ensembles/distributional predictions to represent uncertainty.
148.plan: Posterior and prior variance are exposed; confidence is a simple function of surprise. Calibrate with reliability diagrams.

149.bar: Hybrid rollouts beat symbolic-only and neural-only prediction on stochastic unseen tasks.
149.card_subject: Action-conditioned world models enable imagined futures directly in visual latent space.
149.plan: imagine() exists. Integrate with symbolic world rules through one StateHypothesis.

150.bar: The same object and task are recognised across layouts, scales, themes and transforms without new rules.
150.card_subject: Large visual pretraining encourages representations robust to viewpoint/background variation.
150.plan: Screen geometry adaptation is engineered and brittle. Augmentation and object-centric normalisation.

151.bar: Every world-model result is traceable to a frozen data and model pair.
151.card_subject: Large world-model projects quantify data mixtures, pretraining and downstream transfer.
151.plan: WorldModelDataCard: sources, frames, environments, action coverage, leakage, representation version.

152.bar: A world-model treatment improves success and sample efficiency under equal action budgets.
152.card_subject: V-JEPA-style results tie prediction quality to control performance, not reconstruction loss alone.
152.plan: Matched MPC vs reactive vs symbolic-planner arms on the same observations; matched_budget already refuses unmatched verdicts.

153.bar: A scaling law identifies whether Aura is data-, model- or interface-limited.
153.card_subject: Large projects can study how world-model capability changes with data/model size.
153.plan: Several bounded sizes before further investment. This is 213 applied to the world model.

154.bar: Full Aura closes a meaningful fraction of the frontier gap on held-out tasks at acceptable compute.
154.card_subject: Frontier models generally possess stronger base reasoning and instruction-following than a local 27B-class model.
154.plan: Not a gap to close by imitation. The measurable bar is architecture value-add over the same base model, which is 211 plus 189.

155.bar: Held-out multilingual accuracy improves with no English regression.
155.card_subject: Frontier training covers many languages and scripts at enormous scale.
155.plan: Rebuilding multilingual pretraining locally is out of scope and the report says so. Retrieval and translation tools only.

156.bar: Aura plus 27B beats a 27B scaffold by a large margin on frozen code suites.
156.card_subject: Large frontier systems are stronger on broad code generation/debugging/repo tasks.
156.outstanding: a coding board run: full Aura against the 27B scaffold on a frozen suite
156.plan: The architecture-value-add measurement, on code. Uses executable verification Aura already has.

157.bar: Verified math gains survive base-model and tool-only controls.
157.card_subject: Larger models and specialized reasoning training improve difficult math performance.
157.plan: One math lane: formal solver, RLC operator synthesis, proof checking, with both controls.

158.bar: Cross-modal tasks improve without converting all perception to text.
158.card_subject: Frontier multimodal models jointly represent images/audio/video/text at high quality.
158.plan: Project multimodal encoders into the canonical cognitive vector.

159.bar: Knowledge accuracy and freshness improve while provenance stays explicit.
159.card_subject: Frontier models absorb enormous corpora and current multimodal data.
159.plan: Treat external stores as inspectable semantic memory with source freshness. Already Aura's design; make freshness measurable.

160.bar: Performance stays stable as lifetime memory grows without dumping raw history into context.
160.card_subject: Frontier systems often support larger, better-trained context handling.
160.plan: Retrieval compression and memory distillation with a long-context evaluation. Directly relevant to a lifelong agent.

161.bar: Latency and energy improve at fixed answer quality while continuous organs stay responsive.
161.card_subject: Industrial frontier serving uses highly optimized distributed kernels, batching, cache management and hardware stacks.
161.plan: Only sovereignty-relevant kernels: KV reuse, speculative decoding, quantisation, tier routing.

162.bar: Post-trained cortex improves held-out capability with no catastrophic regression and with provenance.
162.card_subject: Frontier labs use huge preference/reasoning/tool-use datasets and reinforcement/post-training pipelines.
162.plan: Self-generated verified trajectories plus curriculum replay. The verification gate is what makes it safe.

163.bar: Independent red-team findings trend down release over release and fixes are regression-pinned.
163.card_subject: Large labs run broad adversarial evaluations and specialized safety teams.
163.plan: Publish threat-model suites; the regression pinning half is buildable now.

164.bar: Every capability claim is reproducible from a single manifest with matched baselines.
164.card_subject: Frontier labs run large multi-domain automated benchmark/evals farms.
164.plan: One EvalOrchestrator over versioned tasks, baselines, compute accounting, seeds and signed results. Overlaps 210.

165.bar: Several independent replications reproduce key causal effects.
165.card_subject: Widely used models are evaluated by many external groups.
165.plan: Release reproducible canaries and fixed evaluation packs. Requires 164 first.

166.bar: Selected augmentations close probe and task deficits without a larger base model.
166.card_subject: Larger pretrained models may contain more robust broad abstractions simply from training scale.
166.plan: Probe the representational gap, then route deficits to memory, symbolic and world-model systems.

167.bar: Full Aura decomposes unseen tasks better than the 27B baseline and improves with experience.
167.card_subject: Strong frontier reasoning models often infer plans from vague language better than smaller models.
167.outstanding: unseen-task decomposition against the 27B baseline, repeated as experience accumulates
167.plan: Compile recurring decompositions into the W5 Procedure registry; the improvement-with-experience half is the developmental claim.

168.bar: Novel tools need fewer demonstrations and tool-choice accuracy beats static descriptions.
168.campaign_run: 400 trials over 6 tools whose descriptions overlap. Choosing from descriptions alone scores 0.325 against a chance floor of 0.167; choosing from what happened when a tool was used scores 0.995, and reaches ten correct choices in a row after 14 demonstrations (docs/evidence/developmental_campaign.json)
168.card_subject: Frontier models have broad post-training on tool schemas and agentic formats.
168.plan: Learn typed tool affordances and effects from receipts; promote reusable operator schemas.

169.bar: Regression detection catches distribution shift before subjective review.
169.card_subject: Industrial systems correlate latency, failure, model version and user outcomes across huge fleets.
169.plan: A local experiment warehouse with run metrics, version lineage and causal arm labels. Overlaps 164.

170.bar: At least 80 percent of cross-subsystem cognitive handoffs use one contract and duplicate adapters are removed.
170.card_subject: Mature architectures obtain leverage from a small number of canonical interfaces; Aura still has many organ-specific state representations.
170.plan: CognitiveStateRef: identity, time, provenance, uncertainty, ownership, representation links, causal parents. P0 keystone.

171.bar: Synthetic duplicate evidence cannot inflate belief; independent evidence raises confidence predictably.
171.card_subject: NARS/PLN-style systems force evidence semantics to be explicit, while Aura mixes confidence floats, counts, Wilson bounds, model probabilities and receipts.
171.plan: EvidencePacket with source ids, dependence set, mass and merge rules. The single most load-bearing item in the report.

172.bar: Procedures learned by different subsystems are matched, composed, valued and executed through one registry.
172.card_subject: ACT-R, Soar, CLARION and LIDA each gain from procedures being one first-class cognitive currency.
172.plan: Procedure with typed preconditions, program, effects, cost, risk, evidence, provenance and executable backends.

173.bar: One learned concept is traceable across at least four substrates and usable by each without relabeling.
173.card_subject: SPA and OpenCog emphasize representations that can move across mechanisms without losing identity.
173.plan: ConceptHandle plus a projection registry with confidence-preserving conversions.

174.bar: Repeated heterogeneous tasks show falling deliberation cost from automatically acquired procedures.
174.card_subject: ACT-R/Soar/CLARION make repeated deliberation naturally become compiled skill.
174.plan: The trace compiler over W3, emitting into W5. Pairs with the 218 automaticity index as its measurement.

175.bar: Injected impasses in major organs trigger comparable subproblem handling and learning rather than silent fallback.
175.card_subject: Soar turns failure-to-decide into a universal occasion for deeper cognition.
175.plan: One impasse bus; every decision system reports tie, conflict, rejection, no-change and constraint failure.

176.bar: A compiled rule omits irrelevant context while keeping every necessary causal condition across held-out variants.
176.card_subject: Soar EBC identifies which prior conditions actually supported a result.
176.plan: Read-dependency capture on the W3 event, then the minimal support subgraph.

177.bar: Reasoning methods compare under a stable Pareto frontier and a learned stopping policy.
177.card_subject: NARS and ACT-R-like approaches make resource use part of cognitive selection.
177.plan: One normalised CognitiveCost from time, memory pressure, model tier, tool risk and opportunity cost.

178.bar: At matched compute, more work goes to consequential uncertain tasks and total reward rises.
178.card_subject: Resource-rational systems decide whether thinking longer is worth it.
178.plan: The value-of-computation controller over CognitiveCost. Absorbs 015.

179.bar: Reliability diagrams and Brier scores stay calibrated across domains and aggregation improves decisions.
179.card_subject: Competitor traditions validate probabilities/confidence against outcomes.
179.plan: calibration.py already computes Brier. Missing: one calibration layer every uncertainty source passes through.

180.bar: Across three unrelated domains, information-seeking reduces uncertainty and improves later reward against a no-EIG control.
180.card_subject: Active learning should be a universal option when uncertainty matters, not confined to one pursuit path.
180.plan: Expected information gain as an action-value term available to System 2, tool choice, social inquiry and self-testing.

181.bar: One learned policy improves held-out performance at fixed compute with interpretable allocation shifts.
181.card_subject: LIDA/ECAN/modern agents learn what is worth processing.
181.plan: Workspace salience, ECAN and perception priority are three policies. One policy consuming downstream causal value.

182.bar: A strategy learned in A improves B with different surface vocabulary; a shuffled mapping does not.
182.card_subject: CogPrime-like schematic thinking and broad transfer require recognizing shared relations despite surface difference.
182.plan: The shuffled-mapping null is what makes it a result rather than a demo.

183.bar: A skill travels implicit -> explicit -> neural and preserves behaviour within tolerance; each form adds measurable benefit.
183.card_subject: CLARION and SPA/OpenCog together suggest durable cognition needs conversion among tacit skill, explicit rule and neural execution.
183.plan: Extract, Distil, Explain with semantic equivalence tests. W8 is exactly this.

184.bar: The grown-reset gap grows with experience and survives matched memory, context and compute controls.
184.card_subject: The central claim of a developmental architecture is that past life improves future learning.
184.plan: THE decisive experiment. Everything in W1-W8 exists to make its causal chain auditable.

185.bar: Later checkpoints beat earlier ones on transfer tasks, not remembered ones.
185.card_subject: Development should produce a measurable relationship between experience history and competence.
185.plan: Checkpoint one lineage at several ages; evaluate frozen suites with no update during evaluation.

186.bar: At least one learned abstraction reaches the structural-analogue or unrelated-domain tier with causal benefit.
186.card_subject: Strong generality requires transfer beyond superficially similar task signatures.
186.plan: Define the transfer tiers and require every transfer claim to name its tier. Cheap, and it disciplines every other claim.

187.bar: Aura derives a semantic operator absent from the original evaluator, solves a previously unreachable family, and later composes it into another learned operator.
187.card_subject: No compared system fully solves open-ended operator invention either, but Hyperon/MOSES/representation-building approaches highlight the missing level.
187.plan: The deepest item. Requires W10 rollback and sandbox proof first; self-extension without them is untestable self-corruption.

188.bar: A new operator survives adversarial held-out tests and rollback restores exact prior semantics.
188.card_subject: A truly self-extending language needs changes to evaluator semantics to be first-class, testable and reversible.
188.plan: Versioned kernel extensions with effect types, resource bounds, differential tests and automatic rollback.

189.bar: Every retained organ has a capability contribution report or is classified as non-load-bearing.
189.card_subject: Mature science separates causal existence from useful performance contribution.
189.plan: Full vs lesioned vs compute-matched vs random-state, per organ. The machinery exists; the coverage does not.

190.bar: Core subsystem count and dependency entropy fall while benchmarks hold or improve.
190.card_subject: ACT-R/NARS/Soar derive breadth from fewer core principles than Aura.
190.plan: Depends on 189. Merge and delete driven by behavioural equivalence.

191.bar: Claims no longer rest on unidentifiable point estimates and sensitivity reports generate automatically.
191.card_subject: Cognitive modeling requires knowing whether fitted parameters are actually determined by data.
191.plan: ParameterRegistry separating FITTED from POLICY, with bootstrap intervals and sensitivity.

192.bar: Decisive results reproduce from a preregistration hash and post-hoc changes are visible.
192.card_subject: External science reduces researcher degrees of freedom by freezing hypotheses/tests before seeing results.
192.plan: Already built: frozen declaration, content hash, EvidenceStatus. Remaining work is COVERAGE - make it required for designated decisive experiments.

193.bar: Multiple independent machines reproduce core causal effects within declared tolerance.
193.card_subject: The mature comparison systems have broader communities and external validation.
193.plan: Containerised minimal reproductions with signed environment and model hashes. Requires 164.

194.bar: Developmental gains survive tasks unlikely to be memorised and matched base-model controls.
194.card_subject: Foundation-model and transfer research must separate learned priors from evaluation exposure.
194.plan: Procedurally generated private tasks plus a cortex-only baseline. The contamination risk is real for a pretrained cortex.

195.bar: All live environment learners reject transitions without a qualified receipt.
195.card_subject: Embodied learning requires proving that an action changed the intended world, not merely that a tool call succeeded.
195.plan: AutomationReceipt exists for one path. One ActionTransitionReceipt: before-state, authority, observed change, stability, target identity, confidence.

196.bar: The world model and memory refer to the same entity across motion, occlusion and view change.
196.card_subject: World models need stable identity across time/views.
196.plan: EntityTrack ids with observation support, occlusion state, geometry, semantic hypotheses and merge/split lineage.

197.bar: The planner chooses a temporal level and long-horizon predictions beat flat rollout.
197.card_subject: Physical/cognitive environments evolve from milliseconds to days.
197.plan: Fast sensory, action, episode and long-term causal timescales with abstraction links. Overlaps 146.

198.bar: A recovered causal graph predicts unseen interventions better than a correlational model.
198.campaign_run: 40 trials on a linear SCM with hidden confounding, equal rows to both arms. The causal arm recovers a slope of 0.463 against a true effect of 0.400; the correlational arm recovers 1.865, which is the confound. Under unseen interventions the causal arm wins 40 of 40 (RMSE 1.66 against 3.03) while the correlational arm wins 40 of 40 on observations - the reading that would have picked the wrong model (docs/evidence/world_model_campaign.json)
198.card_subject: Strong world understanding requires interventions, not only next-state prediction.
198.plan: Structural causal hypotheses over learned entities, distinguished by intervention.

199.bar: Novel multi-step skills assemble from previously learned components across at least two backends.
199.card_subject: ACT-R/Soar/SPA/Hyperon all benefit when learned components can be reused compositionally.
199.plan: Typed input/output/effect signatures on all procedures plus a composing planner. Follows W5.

200.bar: High-value skills are retained, harmful ones retired, and decision latency stays bounded as experience grows.
200.card_subject: Long-lived architectures must avoid utility collapse as learned knowledge grows.
200.plan: Word ecology and chunk EV are two working economies for two stores. Generalise to all learned artifacts.

201.bar: Developmental gains occur with bounded negative backward transfer and rollback catches damaging updates.
201.card_subject: Continual learning needs explicit forgetting metrics, not just persistence.
201.plan: interference_battery.py is the seed. Report BWT and FWT after every learning block.

202.bar: An offline phase improves future tasks more than a replay-only control without corrupting old competence.
202.card_subject: Biological/cognitive architectures often separate online experience from offline restructuring.

rules.clean_room: Every item is a CLEAN-ROOM adaptation. What is imported is the PROPERTY described in the public literature - an impasse is an occasion for learning, evidence must carry its lineage, a budget has priority and durability. No rival source is read, vendored, translated or paraphrased into this repo, and no rival identifier is adopted where it would carry a licence or imply provenance Aura does not have. Each module names the published description it was built from and states, in its own terms, what Aura does differently and why. This matches the discipline already in core/organism/model_validation.py (OpenWorm/sciunit) and core/cognition/impasse.py (Soar).
rules.gates: make gap-atlas (every card adjudicated, every closed card's test and caller present), make architecture-lint (organ shape rules), make cognitive-complexity (the kernel ratchet, raising it requires a stated reason), plus the existing compile, smoke, lint, writing and layering.
rules.implement_to_what_aura_is: The report prescribes rival-shaped mechanisms. Where Aura already has the property under another name, the work is to unify and prove, not to add a parallel organ. Where the rival's bar does not describe a non-human, non-embodied, single-machine actor, the entry is marked OVERSTATED and the transferable half is stated instead.
rules.section_level_bars: The second review gives ONE acceptance test per section, so 193 of its 194 cards carry a bar that belongs to the section rather than to the card. Every adjudication here addresses the card's own subject - its title and what the rival actually demonstrated, recorded as card_subject - and answers the section bar separately. Five cards where the two point in opposite directions say so explicitly: A8.9 through A8.12 and A12.15, where the card's subject is a rival's deployment result and the section bar is a property Aura can and does implement.
rules.two_reports: Two independent reviews landed on 2026-09-01: a comparative architecture atlas (220 cards, ids 001-220) and a cross-system engineering audit (194 items, ids A1.1-A13.15). They overlap heavily and disagree in places. Both are held here under one adjudication, and where an item appears twice the second entry names the first rather than duplicating the work.

verdicts.OVERSTATED: The bar as written does not transfer; the transferable half is named in the plan.
verdicts.PARTIAL: The mechanism exists; the named property is not established or not universal.
verdicts.PRESENT: Aura already clears the bar; the report is out of date or read the wrong file.

rules.what_closed_means: A card is closed when the bar it names is established by a test that runs, and - where the bar is a claim about the SYSTEM rather than about a module - by a production caller that imports the module. Neither of those is the same as the capability being demonstrated at scale. Nine campaigns are built and have not been run: the developmental grown-versus-reset campaign, the capability board against the bare cortex, the baseline portfolio, the environment bench, continual metrics, the retrieval latency law, world-model calibration, replication on other hardware, and the red-team trend. tools/evidence_report.py names each one and what it would establish, and the claim ladder holds four claims at CAUSAL and none at USEFUL, asserted by a test. The reviews' central finding was that the architecture is ahead of its evidence; this work builds the machinery that measures the gap and does not close it.
